case_title: Varun Chaudhary v. State of Rajasthan
trial_court_outcome: Accused No.1 convicted, Accused Nos. 2 and 3 acquitted
neutral_facts: The victim, an Income Tax Officer, was found dead near his residence. The police arrested three individuals, A-1, A-2, and A-3, and recovered a knife from A-1 and blood-stained clothes from A-3. The trial court convicted A-1 based on the recovered knife, incised wounds on the victim's body, and witness accounts of three persons on a motor cycle. The High Court upheld the conviction of A-1 and also convicted A-2 and A-3. The Supreme Court overturned the convictions, noting that there was no eyewitness, no complete chain of evidence linking the accused to the crime, and the recovered items were not properly proven. The motor cycle's tyre marks were not compared with those at the crime scene, and the knife was never shown to the accused or produced in court.
